 Oral Order
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned APP for the State.

2. Issue notice to the opposite party no.2 by both modes i.e. speed post as well as ordinary post with A/D, for which necessary requisites must be filed on or before 10.11.2023, failing which the quashing application shall stand rejected without further reference to the Bench.
3. Put up this case on 28.02.2024.
4.

In the meantime, the order dated 30.08.2016 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Gaya in Complaint Case No. 577/2016, whereby cognizance of offences under sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code has been taken, shall remain stayed, as it has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that a Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.41155 of 2017(2)
dt.19-10-2023 purely civil dispute has been given a criminal colour, it is next submitted that the sale deed executed by the petitioner, in favour of the O.P. No.2, with respect to the land, in question, had clearly recorded that the petitioner had filed Title Suit No. 113/2008 before the Court of learned Sub-Judge-IV, Gaya, seeking a declaration of title over 19.50 acres of land and confirmation of Ajay Mehta vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147469884/

entities.text: Ajay Mehta vs State Of Bihar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 possession against the State of Bihar and the said suit was decreed in favour of the petitioner by judgment dated 22.12.2011 and decree dated 24.01.2012.
5.

The learned counsel submits that the O.P. No.2 was aware that there was some dispute with respect to the land, which he had purchased from the petitioner, for which, the petitioner had filed the aforesaid title suit thereafter he purchased the said land, the learned counsel next submits that the State of Bihar went in appeal against the judgment and decree passed in T.S. No. 113/2008 but the same also stands decided in favour of the petitioner by judgment dated 01.06.2017.

It is, thus,
submitted that the allegation of the O.P. No.2 herein that the land was sold fraudulently to him has no legs to stand.

(Satyavrat Verma, J) amit/-
